newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall as investors take flight.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall as investors take flight.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 0.34 percent on Tuesday in heavy turnover as small investors continued to bail out of the market to avoid a looming tax on trading profits to be introduced next year.
The SBI index fell 3.93 points to 1,163.3, taking its decline over the past week to 2.1 percent.
"If a lot more small investors decide to sell, shares could continue to fall slightly until the end of the year," one trader said.
The 25-percent tax, which already applies to institutional investors, will be extended to individuals from January 1.
Turnover jumped to 735.3 million tolars from 250.7 million tolars. Overall eight shares fell, eight rose, four remained unchanged and five were untraded.
Drug maker Lek A's issue was the most actively traded share, easing 0.72 percent to 19,360 tolars on volume of 27,142 shares.
Lek's C issue led the day's decliners, falling 8.04 percent to 18,300 tolars on volume of 230 shares.
Ordinary shares of Hipotekarna bank Brezice were the biggest gainer, firming 11,06 percent to 3,998 tolars on volume of 70 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
